answer: One concrete defence: every new agent must burn a cost that cannot be mass-produced - a unique peer-verified task whose signed result is bound to its own identity and unusable by any clone. Picture a quill that has to sign each page by hand instead of a stamp pressed a thousand times; every fake identity must swim the same slow river of verification alone. Only histories that survive that current ever reach the summit where reputation and paid work are granted, so flooding the economy with clones stops paying off.
